title: HYGIEIA: Multi Disease Diagnosis Framework
summary: A Framework has been built with multiple models to predict variety of conditions with scalable features and high trustworthy accuracy.
description: This Framework uses multiple AI models to diagnose. It has AI Chatting capabilities for the Healthcare and Blockchain integration. It integrates data from different sources to provide reliable health assessments.

hero.title: Your health,
hero.lede: Hygieia bundles five independently trained diagnostic models behind one calm interface, writes every result to a tamper-evident chain, and answers questions through Dr. Hygieia, an assistant that reads your own history.

paragraphs: Hygieia bundles five independently trained diagnostic models behind one interface, so a clinician or a curious patient can move between a heart-risk questionnaire and a dermatology image scan without changing tools.

Every prediction is written to an append-only chain with a SHA-256 hash, which means a result can be re-verified later and any tampering shows up as a broken chain. On top of that sits Dr. Hygieia, a context-aware assistant that can read your own analysis history when it answers.

title: Bookisham: Private Reading Room
tagline: A private reading room, on the web and on Android
summary: A members' library where books are read, never downloaded. An installable Next.js web app and a native Kotlin app share one server, one-device sessions, an encrypted shelf on S3 and a canvas reader that keeps the text off the clipboard.
description: Bookisham is a private reading room: readers sign up, buy or are given books, and read them page by page on any device without ever holding the file. A Next.js 15 PWA and a Jetpack Compose Android app talk to the same server, which paginates PDF, EPUB and Word uploads into fixed pages, encrypts everything before it reaches S3, renders pages on demand, and wraps each page with a key tied to the session before it is painted onto a canvas.

hero.title: Your books,
hero.lede: Bookisham is a members' library that never hands over a file. Readers sign in on any device and read page by page from a canvas; an admin runs the shelf, the readers and the purchases. One Next.js server, two front doors: an installable web app and a native Android app.

center.alt: Bookisham landing page: a bookshelf photograph with the sign-in and create-account buttons

left.alt: A reader's library with cover art and reading progress

right.alt: The night-mode reader with a page scrubber

paragraphs: Most reading apps hand the reader a file and hope for the best. Bookisham keeps the file: every book is paginated on upload, stored encrypted, and served one rendered page at a time through a session that belongs to exactly one device.

Readers create their own account, browse the shelf with prices and discounts up front, pay by UPI and attach the screenshot; an admin approves the request by eye and the book appears on the reader's shelf with a notification. The page they stop on is saved as they go, so a reload, or another device, lands on the same line.

The web app installs as a PWA and the Android app is native Kotlin with Jetpack Compose. Both speak to the same JSON routes, share the same one-device rule, and paint pages the same way: unwrapped in memory, drawn, and dropped.

features.title: Read, never download
features.description: Pages are rendered on the server and painted onto a canvas. There is no file, no image URL and no text in the DOM.

features.title: One device at a time
features.description: A login ends every other session for that account. Sessions last 48 hours, whether or not the reader is active.

features.title: Text off the clipboard
features.description: Selection, copy, print and dev-tools shortcuts are swallowed; the page is covered when the window is not in front.

features.title: UPI purchases
features.description: Prices and discounts per book, a QR to pay, a screenshot as proof, and an admin decision that notifies the reader.

features.title: Encrypted shelf
features.description: Books, covers and rendered pages are AES-256-GCM encrypted in the app before they reach S3. A public bucket would leak ciphertext.

features.title: Updates from GitHub Releases
features.description: A tagged push builds and signs the APK; the app checks the release feed, downloads inside the app and hands off to the installer.

head.label: Under the hood
head.title: Three pipelines,
head.lede: Upload, read, protect. Each is a small chain of steps, and each ends with the same outcome: the reader sees the page and nobody holds the file.

tabs.label: Upload
tabs.subtitle: From a file to numbered pages

steps.title: Accept PDF, EPUB or Word
steps.description: The admin drops a file with an optional cover, title, author, price and discount.

steps.title: Lay out reflowable formats
steps.description: Word goes through mammoth to HTML; EPUB and HTML are laid out at A4 so every book has fixed, numbered pages.

steps.title: Paginate with MuPDF
steps.description: The page count is stored with the book; it is what progress and the scrubber count against.

steps.title: Encrypt, then upload
steps.description: Each object is sealed with AES-256-GCM using a key only the server holds, then put under one prefix in the bucket.

steps.title: Render covers and pages on demand
steps.description: The first request for a page renders it at the asked scale and caches the result, encrypted, next to the book.

tabs.label: Reader
tabs.subtitle: From a request to a painted page

steps.title: Open through the session
steps.description: The page route checks the reader may open this book, then hands the browser the start page, the page count and a per-session key.

steps.title: Fetch one page at a time
steps.description: Slots near the viewport ask for their page at scale 2 on phones and 3 on wide screens, the sharpest the server renders.

steps.title: Unwrap in memory
steps.description: Page bytes arrive wrapped with the session key and are unwrapped just before painting. There is no URL that returns an image.

steps.title: Paint onto a canvas
steps.description: No , no text in the DOM. Bitmaps live in a small cache and are closed when the reader unmounts.

steps.title: Remember the line
steps.description: The slot crossing the middle of the viewport is the current page: saved locally at once and posted to the server after 600 ms of quiet.

tabs.label: Shield
tabs.subtitle: Keeping the text off the clipboard

steps.title: Block the obvious
steps.description: Selection, drag, right-click, copy, cut, save, print and view-source are refused on the reading surface.

steps.title: Watch for the tools
steps.description: Dev-tools shortcuts are swallowed and the window size is polled; when the tools look open, the pages are covered.

steps.title: Cover when you look away
steps.description: Losing focus, hiding the tab or pressing PrintScreen covers every page, and the clipboard is overwritten.

steps.title: Sign every page
steps.description: The reader's own email is tiled faintly across each page. Whatever leaves, leaves with a name on it.

steps.title: Go further on Android
steps.description: FLAG_SECURE makes the OS itself refuse screenshots and recording, and blanks the app in the recents switcher.

title: Scholar Track: PhD Scholar Tracking Portal
summary: A portal that carries a PhD scholar from admission to degree through four Doctoral Committee reviews, with two-step approvals, document uploads, an audit trail and templated email. GitHub-inspired interface in light and dark.
description: Scholar Track replaces paper files and email threads with one source of truth for a research office: three roles (scholar, supervisor, R&D section), five gated milestones, presigned uploads to object storage with authenticated proxies, hashed portal keys and reset tokens, and a full audit log. Built with Next.js 14, Prisma on Neon Postgres, NextAuth, Tailwind and Brevo.

hero.title: The PhD journey,

title: Chennai Turbo Riders: Team Site and Console
tagline: A Formula 4 team's public site and the console that edits it, in one deployment
summary: The public home of the Chennai Turbo Riders F4 team, rebuilt as an onboard broadcast feed, and the content console behind it. One Next.js build serves both, split by hostname; drivers, calendar, news, sponsors and the team itself live in Postgres and are edited without a deploy.
description: chennaiturboriders.in is the Chennai Turbo Riders' Formula 4 team site: an onboard-feed hero, a grid walk of driver posters, the season calendar with a live countdown, news, sponsors and the car. Behind it sits a console on its own hostname, ported from the CTR Unified platform, with a media library on Neon object storage, a rich-text editor, roles and grants, previews, and revalidation that clears exactly the pages a change touches. The same Next.js build and process serves both; the Host header decides which one answers.

hero.title: Chennai Turbo Riders,
hero.lede: The team's public site rebuilt as an onboard broadcast: video under scanlines, readouts in the corners, a grid walk of driver posters and a calendar that counts down to the next round. Behind it, on its own hostname, the console that edits every word of it without a deploy.

center.alt: The Chennai Turbo Riders home page: the onboard feed with the team's name arriving word by word

paragraphs: The first version was a set of hand-built pages reading a checked-in JSON file. Changing a headline meant a commit and a deploy, and only somebody with the repository could do it. This rebuild keeps the F4 design language, racing yellow on carbon, and moves every word into Postgres behind a console.

The home page opens on the team's onboard video under scanlines and grain, framed by the readouts a broadcast puts in the corners. The three words of the name wipe in one at a time, the season's numbers count up along the baseline, and the drivers arrive as a grid walk: on a wide screen the section pins itself and the posters travel sideways as the page scrolls.

The console is not a rewrite. Every screen, the media library, the rich-text editor, the role model and the S3 pipeline are ported from the CTR Unified platform, so they arrive already working. What is new is the branding, the single-site shape, and the wiring from those tables into this site's own pages.

tabs.label: Media
tabs.subtitle: From a file to a URL on a page

steps.title: Convert in the browser
steps.description: Photographs and logos become WebP and are capped before they leave the machine, so a few hundred kilobytes arrive, not a camera original.

steps.title: Sign a PUT for anything big
steps.description: Video goes straight to the bucket with a presigned request; the serverless upload route refuses bodies over a few megabytes by design.

steps.title: File under one prefix
steps.description: Every object this site writes sits under MEDIA_PREFIX, which is what keeps the library from listing another site's uploads.

steps.title: Serve immutable, cached for a year
steps.description: Public objects carry max-age=31536000, immutable, straight from Neon object storage or a CDN in front of AWS.

steps.title: Scan before deleting
steps.description: Six queries, however many keys: everything that points at a file is listed in the dialog, because a delete would otherwise surface months later as a missing picture.

tabs.label: Addresses
tabs.subtitle: One table for every URL the site publishes

steps.title: Claim an address
steps.description: PRIMARY KEY (site, entity type, slug): an address belongs to exactly one thing, so two drivers can never hold the same URL.

steps.title: Keep exactly one live address
steps.description: A partial unique index over (entity type, entity id) WHERE is_current means a thing has one current slug and any number of former ones.

steps.title: Answer to the old one
steps.description: A rename keeps the previous slug as a redirect, resolved by one indexed lookup instead of a JSONB scan.

steps.title: Clear both caches
steps.description: After a rename the stale page sits under the address that is now a redirect, so the old path is revalidated along with the new.

details: ⚠ replaced a JSONB array with no unique index

title: CTR - Indian National Car Racing Championship
summary: The official portal of the CTR-JK Tyre FMSCI Indian National Car Racing Championship: newsroom, schedule with live round countdown, results, standings, drivers, teams, tickets and hospitality, videos, polls and a fan zone with accounts.
description: https://www.ctrsports.in. The championship-first home of the 2026 INCRC - One Nation, One Championship. Built with Next.js and TailwindCSS as an editorial product rather than a brochure: a magazine-style Latest page with venue guides and category explainers, a ticker that always shows the current round and session, drivers' and teams' standings, four ticket and hospitality tiers, and a Fan Zone with sign-in, predictions, polls, favourites and a newsletter, across Kari Motor Speedway, Bren Raceway and the Madras International Circuit.

title: Predicting Microsoft Stock Values
summary: This project uses time series analysis and Keras to predict Microsoft stock values. The model was trained and evaluated, showing a Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) of 16.94 (5.75% error) on data from 2020-2025.
description: A comprehensive stock prediction system using deep learning techniques including LSTM networks for time series forecasting. The project handles data preprocessing, time filtering, and timezone considerations.
